articles.title: Haunted houses may bring people closer, but psychological research suggests the bonding really happens on the ride home
articles.summary: People who felt more scared inside a haunted house, and held hands or touched their companions, were more likely to say the experience brought them closer. But interviews suggest much of the bonding may happen in conversations afterward.

articles.title: Older adults with depression tend to have smaller volumes of a specific part of the hippocampus brain region
articles.summary: Older adults with depression tended to have a smaller volume in one part of the hippocampus, a brain region hit early by Alzheimer’s disease. The link did not appear to be explained by Alzheimer’s-related proteins.

articles.title: Higher progesterone is linked to blurrier brain signals for emotional control, study finds
articles.summary: Women with higher natural progesterone levels showed less distinct brain activity patterns when overriding automatic emotional impulses, according to a neuroimaging study of 116 young women. Estradiol, the other major ovarian hormone, showed no such link.

articles.title: To Keep or Not to Keep: Learning KV Cache Retention in Disaggregated LLM Serving Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disaggregated \textsc{LLM} serving separates prefill and decode across node pools, placing a network fabric between \textsc{KV}-cache computation and consumption. This breaks a key assumption of classical cache policies: a miss no longer incurs only local recomputation, but also network transfer to the decode node. Likewise, admitting a block to the global cache requires an additional transfer, so poor retention decisions waste both memory and bandwidth. articles.title: Interaction-Gated Time-Frequency Learning for Parameter-Efficient PPG-Based Heart Rate Estimation
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) enables low-cost and non-invasive heart rate (HR) monitoring but remains sensitive to waveform distortion, physiological variability, and measurement interference. Temporal waveform characteristics and frequency-domain periodicity provide complementary information for HR estimation; however, effectively exploring and integrating these representations within a compact model remains challenging. This paper proposes TF-IG, a parameter-efficient interaction-gated time-frequency learning framework for PPG-based HR estimation

articles.title: New biological marker could end trial and error in depression care
articles.summary: A new study identifies a stable, brain-derived RNA molecule in the bloodstream that accurately predicts whether a patient will respond to common SSRI antidepressants, potentially saving months of trial-and-error treatments.

articles.title: How long does it take to feel forgiven by God? New study tracks Christians day by day after wrongdoing
articles.summary: Believing God is forgiving isn’t the same as feeling forgiven. A 16-day study of Christians found that a close, less conflicted relationship with God predicted faster gains in feeling pardoned after a wrongdoing, while beliefs about God did not.

articles.title: Kids’ aggression appears to shape parents’ discipline more than the reverse, study finds
articles.summary: Inconsistent discipline is often blamed for aggressive behavior in children. But a study of Norwegian extended families and U.S. adoptive families suggests the arrow may point the other way: aggressive children may make parents less consistent.

articles.title: Beneath psilocybin’s apparent brain chaos, scientists find signs of a hidden order
articles.summary: Psilocybin is often described as throwing the brain into disorder. A new study in Nature suggests that beneath the apparent chaos, brain activity becomes organized around what a person is doing, especially in those who feel a sense of unity.

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising secret behind the human brain’s wrinkles
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered why common marmosets have unusually small, smooth brains despite starting development much like other primates. The secret lies in subtle changes to brain-building cells that slow neuron production, revealing new clues about how the large, folded human brain evolved.

articles.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
articles.summary: A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage. Researchers suspect that getting these nutrients through a healthy diet may offer benefits that supplements alone cannot provide.

articles.title: Intelligence predicts charitable giving and voting in massive Swedish study
articles.summary: A massive analysis of Swedish administrative records reveals that higher cognitive abilities strongly predict prosocial behaviors. Individuals with higher general intelligence are consistently more likely to donate to charity, vote in elections, and buy environmentally friendly vehicles.
